facts.raw_span: A 68-year-old retired man with no prior medical history
presented with two months of dorsal spine pain
gradually progressive motor weakness of the left lower extremity
his weakness acutely worsened, rendering him unable to stand or walk without assistance
there was no history of trauma
spastic paraparesis with weakness of the quadriceps, hamstrings, ankle dorsiflexors, and toe extensors on the left
Patellar and ankle jerks were increased, with sustained clonus at the left ankle and bilateral Babinski signs
Superficial hypoesthesia was present below the T7 level
bladder and bowel function were preserved
a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass posterolateral to the right side of the spinal cord at C7–T1, causing marked canal stenosis and cord deformation
the lesion was intermediate in signal intensity on T1-weighted images and homogeneously low in signal on T2-weighted images
it demonstrated a thin rim of enhancement with no internal enhancement on fat-saturated postcontrast T1-weighted images
